newsitem.title: UK: Middle East dirty tankers steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Middle East dirty tankers steady to firmer.

text.p: Middle East dirty tanker rates were steady to slightly firmer on Tuesday on a shortage of tonnage, brokers said.
"There is quite a bit going on, especially to the east, but a lot of it is P&C (private and confidential) and rates are not that easy to determine," one broker said.
"But the market is quite strong...on a lack of tonnage," he added.
He said very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan were being fixed at about W62.5/64, to Singapore at around W50 and to Europe at about W50/52.5 -- up to 2.5 points up from Monday.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf and transatlantic voyages were also steady at around W62.5, with 130,000 tonne vessels at W95 for the former and W90 from Europe, brokers said.
The 80,000 tonne Mediterranean market, which soared last month from about W100 to as high as W170, remained fairly firm at about W130.
"There are quite a few cargoes on the market but it's a bit volatile...At the moment owners seem able to resist the offers they have been getting," an Italian broker said.
Cross-Med 130,000 tonne vessels remained steady at W95.

The inter-U.K./Cont sector was slightly weaker at about W100 for 80,000 tonne ships. "It's down to a lack of enquiry and a lot of Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) have been used, making more Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) available," one broker said.

Inter-U.K./Cont 20,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were slightly firmer at W210 against W205 on Monday on good interest from the Baltic, the U.K. and northern France. But fuel oil in the Med was hard to assess with few fixtures seen, another broker said.
In the Caribbean, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes Caribs/upcoast edged down to W145/150 on a lack of activity, with 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels slightly lower at W160/165, U.S. brokers said.
